content: 1. When a customer asks for specific technical specs, never stall or promise future testing. If you don't know, immediately use a web search or consult a colleague. In a store, you can also grab a demo unit and test together on the spot.

2. For in-store sales, always leverage the physical environment: invite the customer to test the device themselves, show sample files, and compare side-by-side with competitors. Never send the customer to check online later.

3. If a web search tool fails, do not repeat the same failed action. Switch to another source (e.g., printed spec sheet, call a product specialist) or offer a live demo to answer the question empirically.
4. Use reflection paraphrase early to confirm the customer's dealbreakers, then immediately address them with concrete evidence. Avoid repeating the same promise multiple times.

5. For high-skepticism customers, build trust by admitting what you don't know and then taking immediate, visible action to find the answer (e.g., 'Let's look it up together on the official site right now').

name: Live Demo Verification Tactic
condition: When a customer asks for a spec you don't know, and you have a demo unit available.
example: Instead of promising a video later, say: 'Let's test it right now on this unit. I'll open GoPaint and we can export a file to see how layers are handled.'

name: Immediate Web Search Together Tactic
condition: When a customer asks for a spec and you have internet access in-store.
example: Say: 'Let's look it up together on the official site. I'll open consumer.huawei.com/jp right now.' This builds trust and shows transparency.

name: Dealbreaker Confirmation Loop Tactic
condition: When a customer repeatedly asks for the same information.
example: Paraphrase their concern: 'So the two specs that are dealbreakers for you are X and Y, correct?' Then immediately take action to address both, one at a time.

objection: Customer asks for PSD layer structure and per-brush pressure curve specs.
rebuttal_template: I understand those specs are critical for you. Let's check the official Huawei Japan website together right now on this tablet. [Open browser and search] Here, it shows that GoPaint exports PSD with layer groups preserved. And for pressure curves, let me open the GoPaint settings on this demo unit and we can test it together. See, you can adjust per-brush pressure sensitivity here.

objection: Customer says 'I'll go check reviews myself'.
rebuttal_template: I completely respect that. Before you go, let me show you one quick thing on this demo unit that the reviews might not cover. [Demonstrate a key feature] If you still want to check reviews, I can also send you a direct link to the official spec page on consumer.huawei.com/jp right now.

objection: Customer complains about not getting hard numbers.
rebuttal_template: You're right to ask for hard numbers. I apologize for the delay. Let me pull up the official spec sheet from our system right now. [Show printed or digital spec] Here are the exact numbers: PSD export supports up to 100 layers with folder structure preserved, and per-brush pressure curve is adjustable in GoPaint v2.1. Let me also demonstrate it on this unit.
